completion_conditions: One shared predicate decides the gate, and both cmd_dispatch_check and dispatchable_task_ids consult it.
A high/critical task whose contract is registered on the remote default branch and unchanged on the seven governance fields is dispatchable on both surfaces.
A high/critical task whose contract is absent from, or diverges from, the remote default branch is refused on both surfaces, with a named reason.
The comparison is over exactly mergegate_check._NORMAL_PATH_GOVERNANCE_FIELDS, imported rather than redeclared, so the immutability gate and the dispatch gate cannot drift.
The gate fails closed: when registration cannot be verified, it refuses instead of dispatching.
Low and medium risk keep dispatching from local state, without consulting the remote.
A binder test proves both surfaces agree on the same task in both the admit and the refuse case, and fails if either surface is changed without the other.

SADR-0015's "What shipped, and when." paragraph stops claiming the pre-dispatch gate shipped 2026-07-27 through 2026-07-29, records that it was deferred there as an explicit non-goal, and records where it actually shipped.
The full Python suite, validate_shiki, and the dispatch-exercising shell suites stay green.
CCA verdict and MergeGate evidence are recorded before completion.

decisions: The gate is absent from both code paths, measured not inferred. cmd_dispatch_check (scripts/shiki_tasks.py:1189,1198) sets guardian_required from risk_level and appends "guardian approval required for high/critical risk" unconditionally, with no branch that can clear it; dispatchable_task_ids (scripts/shiki_runtime.py:236) never reads risk_level at all (grep -c risk_level scripts/shiki_runtime.py == 0). shiki_loop.py's four risk_level uses are all merge-time (auto-merge eligibility at :349 and :473), never dispatch-time. Live reproduction: T-20260822T103718387283Z-2f3b0b54 is risk high, its contract is present at origin/main, and dispatch check still returns the blocker.

It was deferred, never descoped. T-20260727T005125902419Z-6c2db440 — the task that delivered the registration half in the 2026-07-27..29 window SADR-0015 credits — carries "The pre-dispatch gate or the envelope ceiling" as an explicit non_goal, and its source plan P-20260727T005119007135Z-1fa476be repeats it. No later Goal picked the gate up. Unlike the Scope Envelope ceiling, which G-20260801T040836630398Z-f28167e5 descoped on the record, no descope record exists for the gate. The remedy is therefore to implement it, and to correct a shipped-claim that was never true — not to descope.

The shared predicate lives in scripts/shiki_tasks.py beside evaluate_lock_grant. This is the precedent set by T-20260805T034218808409Z-0f0d9640 ("Make a granted lock a precondition of dispatch"), which solved the same drift between the same two surfaces: shiki_runtime.py already imports from shiki_tasks, so no import cycle is introduced, and no new module means no scripts/shiki_installer.py manifest entry and no tests/test_install_completeness.py change.

The seven governance fields are imported from mergegate_check._NORMAL_PATH_GOVERNANCE_FIELDS, never redeclared — the single-constant discipline scripts/shiki_contract_approval.py already documents, so the fields a PR may not change are exactly the fields the gate compares. Measured: none of mergegate_check's imports (shiki_contracts, shiki_evidence, shiki_guardian, shiki_jsonschema, shiki_locks, shiki_manifest, shiki_schema) reference shiki_tasks, so the import forms no cycle.

Governance-fields-only comparison is load-bearing, and the measurement confirms SADR-0015's reasoning. try_acquire_locks flips status to "ready" and appends a lock ledger id before dispatch, while a registered contract is still "planned": measured 2026-08-24, 14 of the 19 non-done high/critical tasks are status "planned" on origin/main. A whole-file comparison could never succeed and would leave the gate permanently closed.

Blast radius is zero today. Simulating the gate against live state: all 19 non-done high/critical tasks have their contract on origin/main, and all 19 show zero drift across the seven fields, so the gate would admit every one of them and block none. Enforcing it now costs no in-flight work.

Lock sufficiency was measured, not estimated. A throwaway prototype of the predicate and both call sites was applied in worktree bold-sinoussi-725d46 and then reverted: the full Python suite (1185 tests), validate_shiki, and the module_boundaries, control_plane, run_orchestrator, daemon_runner, loop_lock_guard, goal_loop and runner_claude shell suites all stayed green. No existing test binds either surface's current behaviour — which is exactly why the two could drift, and why the binder test is the missing pairing rather than an extra.

The prototype also proved the satisfaction path the CLI has never had: with the gate applied, dispatch check on T-20260822T103718387283Z-2f3b0b54 drops the guardian blocker entirely and returns only its outstanding lock blocker.

The record correction is a second, dependent task. The corrected paragraph asserts that the gate shipped, which is true only once the code lands, and separating it isolates the docs/adr/SADR-0015 lock — which collides with the in-flight descope task T-20260822T103718387283Z-2f3b0b54. Both tasks are status planned, so the collision is a serialization point, not a present conflict.

docs/agents/decision-control.md belongs to the code task, not the record task. Its Dispatch Guard section prints the exact shape cmd_dispatch_check emits and states "If any field is false, the runtime must not edit files"; the gate changes that shape and retires guardian_approval_required as a blocking field. Its lock collides with critical task T-20260822T102714799429Z-c43ccdcf, also planned — again a serialization point. decision-control.md:61 ("risk level does not require unresolved Guardian approval") already states the requirement and becomes true when this lands, so its wording needs no change.

scripts/shiki_tasks.py collides with five planned tasks (T-20260822T095306178275Z-0dc8a0b4, T-20260801T041653424169Z-07860c35, T-20260822T095306177744Z-38bafdfb, T-20260801T041653348713Z-6283adcd, T-20260822T095306176491Z-a152348c). It is a central module and lock serialization is the intended mechanism; none holds an active grant today.

AMENDMENT, blocking finding 1: the originally frozen scope gated the wrong surfaces. Measured - `grep -c 'dispatchable_task_ids|cmd_dispatch_check' scripts/shiki_loop.py` returns 0; shiki_loop.py:30 imports only {dispatch_runner_task, resolve_default_branch_ref, session_lease_state}; dispatchable_task_ids has exactly ONE production caller (cmd_runner_next, the advisory `shiki runner next`); cmd_dispatch_check is wired only at shiki_cli.py:383, reached by no CI job, workflow, shell suite or loop path. Shipping the contract as frozen would have satisfied all 19 acceptance checks while leaving autonomous dispatch ungated - reproducing the exact 'documented but unenforced' defect SADR-0015 exists to close. dispatch_runner_task (shiki_runtime.py:523) is the real chokepoint and already refuses on evaluate_lock_grant at :545-547; it is now the PRIMARY enforcement site. The Goal's own cited precedent T-20260805T034218808409Z-0f0d9640 gated five surfaces including this one.

AMENDMENT, blocking finding 2: gating the real dispatcher requires path:tests/test_session_lease.py in the locks. Its DispatchEnv fixture (:357-384) declares risk_level high at :377 and :380, points origin at an unreachable https remote at :371, and drives the real dispatch_runner_task four times (:407, :421, :437, :449). A fail-closed gate refuses all four. The remedy is proven by tests/test_repair_delivery.py:76-145, which pushes the task file to a local bare remote and pins origin/HEAD explicitly.

AMENDMENT, hardening 1: resolve_default_branch_ref must be WRAPPED, not adopted. It iterates `for ref in (f'origin/{name}', name)` (shiki_runtime.py:369-376) and falls back to the LOCAL branch, which the implementation runtime can write - the class SADR-0015's Alternatives explicitly rejects. Taken verbatim the gate would FAIL OPEN. It also discards the fetch returncode at :368, shiki_process.run passes no timeout, and a missing git raises FileNotFoundError rather than ShikiError, so a narrow `except ShikiError` fail-closed handler still tracebacks.

AMENDMENT, hardening 2: gate applicability resolves from max(local risk, registered risk) when a registered contract exists. Reading the trigger from the local risk field alone lets a high->medium downgrade suppress the comparison that would detect the downgrade - the bypass SADR-0015's Context names. The existing countermeasure (mergegate_check resolved_guardian_risk_never_weaker) is merge-time and base-anchored, not pre-dispatch. Second-order today because sync_contract_into_worktree (shiki_runtime.py:468, called at :600) makes the coordinator mirror authoritative, so the attack needs a write to the coordinator; the one-line hardening closes it.

AMENDMENT, hardening 3: the refusal reason must avoid the word 'divergence'. tests/test_lock_lifecycle.py:314-315 counts blocking reasons containing it and asserts exactly one; a second occurrence breaks a test outside this task's locks. The reason must instead name the Contract-PR remedy and warn about a stranded lock, because _unblock_ready_tasks (shiki_loop.py:935-957) acquires the lock and flips planned->ready BEFORE any dispatch decision, while `shiki lock release` refuses a non-done task (shiki_tasks.py:1041, :1107).

Sequencing, unchanged and load-bearing: this Contract PR must land FIRST. Both of this Goal's own task contracts are absent from origin/main until it merges, so once the gate ships it would refuse the very work that implements it. Re-measured 2026-08-24: 156 task files, 121 done, 35 non-done, 21 non-done high/critical - 19 present on origin/main with zero drift, 2 absent (this Goal's own two), 0 unequal. The earlier count of 19 predated this Goal's own registration; the substance holds - zero backfill, zero in-flight work blocked.

Rejected by the synthesis, recorded so it is not re-proposed: one exploration dimension recommended keeping the gate OFF dispatch_runner_task to preserve a green tests/test_session_lease.py and recording the loop bypass as a documented boundary. Preserving a green suite by shipping a gate that gates nothing the loop uses inverts the priority; the correct resolution is the lock amendment plus the proven repair_delivery fixture recipe.

Reported, outside every lock, not actioned here: .shiki/goals/G-20260729T065622761503Z-4479b0d3.json and .shiki/plans/P-20260726T053204320783Z-2265e5c3.json both assign 'the dispatch gate' to G-20260725T112636727659Z-23ba3b56, a Goal deleted from the mirror on 2026-07-27 (commit 53b90a8). An agent reading them could conclude the gate is owned elsewhere. Live owner is this Goal.

Reported, outside every lock: docs/agents/control-commands.md:236 and docs/agents/implementation-policy.md:342 both assert that an implementer may not edit files until `dispatch check` is green, but nothing invokes `dispatch check` in CI, the loop, or any workflow. Wiring the gate into dispatch_runner_task makes the SUBSTANCE of those sentences true even though the named command stays advisory.

Changing the merge-time Contract Approval carry (shiki_contract_approval.evaluate_contract_approval) or either of its two consumers. That half shipped 2026-08-01 and is out of scope.
Implementing the Scope Envelope size ceiling. It is a frozen non-goal of G-20260801T040836630398Z-f28167e5 and its descope record is owned by G-20260822T103718385731Z-f0b5eff6.
Editing CONTEXT.md. Its Scope Envelope entry belongs to the in-flight descope task T-20260822T103718387283Z-2f3b0b54, which holds that lock.
Rewriting SADR-0015's Context section. It records the problem as it stood at decision time and stays as history; only the shipped-record claim is corrected.
Changing how risk_level is resolved anywhere, or lowering any task's risk.
Changing the Contract PR path, contract mode, goal_reconcile, or task registration.

Backfilling or re-registering contracts for existing tasks. Measured 2026-08-24: all 19 non-done high/critical tasks already carry their contract on origin/main with zero governance-field drift, so the gate admits all 19 and no backfill is needed.

Authoring a spec_freeze block, Guardian approval evidence, a CCA verdict, or any other approval record. Approval is reserved to its authority (AGENTS.md Approval Records). outcome: A high/critical task is dispatchable only when its contract is registered on the remote default branch and agrees with local state on the seven frozen governance fields, decided once by a shared predicate that BOTH the advertised surface (shiki_runtime.dispatchable_task_ids) and the CLI readiness surface (shiki_tasks.cmd_dispatch_check) consult, so the advertised and enforced sets cannot drift. Measured 2026-08-24 in worktree bold-sinoussi-725d46: `grep -c risk_level scripts/shiki_runtime.py` returns 0, and `shiki dispatch check T-20260822T103718387283Z-2f3b0b54` returns "guardian approval required for high/critical risk" as a blocker with no satisfaction path even though that task's contract is present at origin/main (registered by Guardian-approved Contract PR #341, merge commit 2d7a193). SADR-0015's "What shipped, and when." paragraph therefore claims a gate that no code path implements, and the record is corrected to say what actually happened.

amendments: 2026-08-24: operator-approved Spec Amendment, applied before the Contract PR merged. Triggered by the CI-08 Workflow parallel exploration sweep (run wf_8c96304b-90e), which returned NOT SOUND AS CONTRACTED because the frozen scope named cmd_dispatch_check and dispatchable_task_ids exhaustively and neither is on the path that starts an implementer session. Amended: task 1's scope now names dispatch_runner_task (scripts/shiki_runtime.py:523) as the PRIMARY enforcement site and adds three hardenings (refuse when origin/<default> is unverifiable rather than falling back to the writable local branch; resolve gate applicability from max(local, registered) risk; forbid the word 'divergence' in the refusal reason); task 1's locks gain path:tests/test_session_lease.py; task 1's acceptance_checks grow from 19 to 26 and its non_goals from 10 to 14. Unchanged: risk_level, required_skills, test_command, task 2 in full, and the seven-governance-field comparison. The operator approved this amendment in the Claude Code planning session on 2026-08-24, choosing 'Amend: blocking + hardenings' over amending only the blocking findings or merging the contract as frozen.
spec_freeze.source: Operator approved the drafted requirements in the Claude Code planning session on 2026-08-24, answering the Spec Freeze question with 'Approve - freeze and register'. Earlier in the same session the operator chose to implement the gate and correct the record, over a documentation-only correction, after being shown that the gate was deferred as an explicit non_goal of T-20260727T005125902419Z-6c2db440 rather than descoped on the record, and that enforcing it would admit all 19 live high/critical tasks and block none. The frozen requirements were reviewed alongside the live reproduction on T-20260822T103718387283Z-2f3b0b54 (contract present at origin/main via merged Contract PR #341, dispatch check still blocked with no satisfaction path), the measured lock-sufficiency run in worktree bold-sinoussi-725d46 (prototype applied and then reverted: 1185 tests, validate_shiki and seven dispatch-exercising shell suites all green, and no existing test binding either surface's behaviour), the two-task split and its dependency, the five-lock set, and the two named lock collisions with planned tasks.

acceptance_checks: scripts/shiki_tasks.py defines a single predicate returning (satisfied, reason) that decides the SADR-0015 pre-dispatch gate, and it is the only place that decision is made.

That predicate obtains the compared field list from mergegate_check._NORMAL_PATH_GOVERNANCE_FIELDS; scripts/shiki_tasks.py declares no second copy of the seven field names, and a test binds the compared set to that imported constant so a future edit to either cannot silently diverge.

scripts/shiki_runtime.py dispatch_runner_task refuses a high/critical task whose contract is absent from or unequal to the remote default branch, raising ShikiError with the predicate's reason, in the same style as the existing evaluate_lock_grant refusal at :545-547. A test drives the real dispatch_runner_task for both the admit and the refuse case.

The gate is enforced on the Goal Loop's dispatch path: `grep -c 'dispatchable_task_ids\|cmd_dispatch_check' scripts/shiki_loop.py` still returns 0, and a high/critical task with no registered contract is nevertheless refused when dispatched through dispatch_runner_task.

cmd_dispatch_check consults the predicate, and the string "guardian approval required for high/critical risk" is no longer emitted as an unconditional blocker. Measured before the change: `shiki dispatch check T-20260822T103718387283Z-2f3b0b54` returns it even though that task's contract is present at origin/main.
shiki dispatch check on a high/critical task whose contract is registered and unchanged returns that task's contract-gate field as satisfied and does not list the gate among blocking_reasons.
dispatchable_task_ids consults the SAME predicate and omits a high/critical task the predicate refuses.

A binder test in tests/test_dispatch_contract_registration.py proves ALL THREE surfaces agree on ONE task in BOTH directions: registered and unchanged means dispatch check reports dispatchable, the id appears in dispatchable_task_ids, and dispatch_runner_task proceeds; absent or unequal means dispatch check reports not dispatchable, the id does not appear, and dispatch_runner_task refuses. The test fails if any one surface is changed without the others.
A high/critical task whose contract exists on the remote default branch and is equal on all seven governance fields is SATISFIED by the predicate.
A high/critical task whose contract is absent from the remote default branch is REFUSED, with a reason naming the task and the ref consulted.
For each of the seven governance fields individually, a high/critical task unequal on that field alone is REFUSED, with a reason naming that field.
A high/critical task whose registered contract differs ONLY on status, expected_pr or ledger_evidence is SATISFIED, proving the comparison is governance-fields-only and not whole-file.
A task whose effective risk is low or medium is SATISFIED without consulting the remote default branch.
Effective risk is max(local, registered) when a registered contract exists: a task recorded high on the remote but lowered to medium locally is still gated, and a test pins that case.

The predicate REFUSES when origin/<default> cannot be verified and never accepts the local branch as a substitute; a test proves a repository whose local default branch exists but whose origin/<default> does not is refused, not admitted.

The predicate fails closed on every verification failure: unresolvable default branch, failed or unavailable git, and an unparseable registered contract each return NOT satisfied with a named reason. No input returns satisfied by default.

The refusal reason names the Contract-PR remedy and warns that an already-acquired lock may need manual release, and contains no occurrence of the word "divergence"; tests/test_lock_lifecycle.py passes unchanged, including its assertion that exactly one blocking reason contains that word.

tests/test_session_lease.py passes with its DispatchEnv fixture rebuilt on the tests/test_repair_delivery.py recipe, and its four dispatch_runner_task calls still exercise the real dispatcher at risk high.

docs/agents/decision-control.md's Dispatch Guard JSON example matches the fields cmd_dispatch_check emits after this change, including blocking_reasons, and its surrounding prose no longer implies that guardian_approval_required: true alone forbids dispatch.
docs/agents/decision-control.md line 61 ("risk level does not require unresolved Guardian approval") is unchanged.
The predicate's docstring records that orchestrate_plan's own dispatchable list is DELIBERATELY not gated, and why.
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests passes.
python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target . passes.

scripts/test_shiki_module_boundaries.sh, test_shiki_control_plane.sh, test_shiki_run_orchestrator.sh, test_shiki_daemon_runner.sh, test_shiki_loop_lock_guard.sh, test_shiki_goal_loop.sh and test_shiki_runner_claude.sh all pass.
git diff --name-only against the merge base lists only files inside the declared locks.
scripts/shiki_guardian.py and scripts/shiki_contract_approval.py are byte-identical to their base versions.
non_goals: Modifying scripts/shiki_guardian.py, evaluate_guardian_approval, or any of the four existing approval sources. The pre-dispatch gate is a dispatch precondition, not an approval source.
Modifying scripts/shiki_contract_approval.py or either consumer of the merge-time Contract Approval carry.
Editing docs/adr/SADR-0015-contract-approval-before-dispatch.md. The record correction is the second task of this Goal and holds that lock.

Editing CONTEXT.md, which is held by the in-flight descope task T-20260822T103718387283Z-2f3b0b54. Its Contract PR entry already states the gate as domain law and becomes true on ship; it needs no edit.
Changing docs/agents/decision-control.md line 61; it already states the requirement this task makes true.
Changing how risk_level is resolved at MERGE time, or lowering any task's risk. The max(local, registered) resolution added here decides only whether the pre-dispatch gate APPLIES.

Gating scripts/shiki_tasks.py orchestrate_plan's own `dispatchable` list (:646-664). A freshly registered contract is by definition not yet on the remote, so gating plan registration would empty the dispatchable set for every high/critical plan and deadlock registration itself. Record the exclusion explicitly in the predicate docstring so it reads as deliberate rather than missed.
Extending tests/test_dispatch_lock_precondition.py in place. It carries the lock-precondition binder; the contract-registration binder belongs in the new tests/test_dispatch_contract_registration.py.

Modifying .shiki/schemas/dispatch-guard.schema.json. Its `required` already lists guardian_approval_required and blocking_reasons and it sets additionalProperties: true, so it already admits the new field; it is outside the declared locks.
Widening the compared set beyond the seven governance fields - notably to `dependencies`. DAG integrity is a separate concern; state it as out of scope in the docstring rather than silently widening.
Declaring a second copy of the seven governance field names. The list is imported from mergegate_check or the task is not done.

Adding a new module, and therefore adding any scripts/shiki_installer.py manifest entry or tests/test_install_completeness.py change. The predicate belongs beside evaluate_lock_grant in scripts/shiki_tasks.py.
Registering, backfilling, re-registering or otherwise mutating any contract under .shiki/tasks. Measured: no backfill is required.

Authoring a spec_freeze block, Guardian approval evidence, a CCA verdict, or any other approval record. An acceptance criterion that cannot be satisfied with the artifacts present in the worktree must be reported as a stop, never closed by manufacturing the missing artifact.
